criteria.name: Thumb-stop cover
criteria.notes: 'The robot is in Ketchikan. The stroke reader is everywhere.' is 10 words, a real named tension, set at 76px Fraunces in ink at 14.2:1, and it fits 3/3 lines. The high-key cotton-rag register is the first white deck in nine runs and will genuinely stop a scroll in a feed of dark decks. Held off 9: there is no number anywhere on the cover, the subhead band 'TWELVE BOROUGHS CUT OUT OF ONE STATE SHEET' reads as a second text mass at 432px, and the twelve lifted tiles resolve at thumb scale as a scatter of small gold ticks rather than one gesture, which is exactly the risk the cartographer's own dossier flagged at item 13. The bottom fifth of the frame is near-uniform paper; the Gulf emboss is present but at very low amplitude.

criteria.name: Story arc & swipe momentum
criteria.notes: Clean beat structure and slide 02 pays instantly with 185 / eight / $181.9M / 1 DOLLAR IN 15. Loops are planted and paid: 'which eight' opens on 01 and closes on 06; 'what does a placeless award look like' opens on 03 and pays on 04; slide 07 carries an explicit forward hook, 'Next, the four at true width.' The contact sheet reads as one composed sequence in one register. Held off 9 because 06 and 07 are two consecutive reference/meta frames and momentum sags across them, and because the argument's punchline ('THE ONE THAT WOULD ACT ALONE BOUGHT A PLANNING YEAR.') lands on 06, which leaves 08's turn as a second, quieter climax about timing. Slide 04 remains the thinnest beat and is reorderable with 05 without much loss.

criteria.name: Artwork craft & genuine detail
criteria.notes: Real strengths: per-edge cabinet extrusion of true projected polygons with outward-facing tests, full-resolution fjords on slide 03 that survive the zoom test beautifully, 185 individually drawn comb rules asserted at render time, the radial aspect hachure on 05, the engraved rose and bezel on 09, deckle and cockle on 06, 64 percent drawn share and 0.250 median pairwise similarity. The dossier ARGUES flat deliberately and measures it (AK.reliefShade stddev 16.8 and never below 170/255 against AKENGRAVE.surface at 62.1 reaching 30), so the rendered-ladder clause is satisfied by argument rather than dodged. But descriptor 7's 'one slide leans on a default or has dead zones' is met by three: slide 08's seam, after four rebuilds, still reads at 1080 as a row of flat yellow rectangles with white tops over a grey smear, with no visible per-tile thickness variation and roughly eight readable blocks where twelve are asserted; slide 07's 'density ramp hatching inside each round bar' shipped as a hatched picture-frame around a knockout plate, so the quantity it encodes is barely legible and the four bars read as four identical boxes at thumb; slides 01 and 03 still carry large near-uniform paper regions in their lower bands. Slide 09's twelve-kerf count block is an ISOTYPE caption, not a modelled object. Consistent physics and line-weight hierarchy are genuinely good; 'zero flat-lazy regions' is not met.

criteria.name: Story-art fusion
criteria.notes: The best criterion in the deck and machine-verified rather than asserted. Comb block widths on 02 and 08 are proportional to the four rounds' dollars; 185 rules counted by assertion, not by loop bound; eight blue strikes at true notification positions with the 0/2/5/1 distribution held by assertion, which makes C35 a DRAWN fact rather than a stated one; slide 06's bars are strictly linear at one pixel per $14,000 so Kodiak is a real 2px tick against Ketchikan's long bar and the 256-to-1 range IS the argument; the empty third column is a milled physical channel; the misregistered second press pass on 04 is the statewide claim as a picture, with both passes now stroked from one decimated Path2D so it is a displacement and not a different outline; the phantom dash on 05 is the planning award. One literal anchor per composition throughout. Held off 10 because slides 01, 04 and 09 are guessable as 'some regions are marked' rather than as this story, and because the cut-and-lift metaphor equates 'named in a service area' with 'a machine landed here', an elision the copy has to correct.

criteria.name: Alaska authenticity & local relevance
criteria.notes: Named orgs, places and numbers throughout: PeaceHealth Ketchikan, Alaska Stroke Coalition, Maniilaq, Mat-Su Regional, Tanana Chiefs, SILC, Kodiak Community Health Center, MapHabit, ACUASI at UAF. Geography is accurate from assets/geo/alaska-boroughs.geo.json at true projection, the Aleutian bleed is labelled 'ALEUTIAN CHAIN CONTINUES WEST' rather than silently cropped, and the deck refuses to dot 42 villages it has no coordinates for, putting them in an ISOTYPE reserve instead. The 5-to-14-day winter medication delay and the four-boroughs-across-water framing are things an Alaskan recognises. Held off 9 because there is no person anywhere in the deck, no voice from a clinic, no single Alaskan whose day changes; it is an accurate catalogue of a spreadsheet, which lands closer to 'would make an Alaskan feel accurately recorded' than 'feel seen'. Slide 05's '5 TO 14 DAYS, WINTER' dimension call also sits over the Southeast panhandle on an Interior slide.

criteria.name: Legibility & platform fitness
criteria.notes: Vector PDF at 5.14 MB inside the 2 to 25 MB band with a 24-character title; nine slides; NN / 09 counters on all nine; qa.py 0 fails and 0 warns including its size and safe-zone checks; every fitted head lands at its declared line count. But this is more than one squeaker. On a white ground the deck's instrument tier is far weaker than the same tier was on the dark decks: graphite #93A0A8 sits at about 2.4:1 and #6B7885 at 3.94:1, and that tier carries information a reader is meant to be able to check, including slide 03's two-line provenance ('MONEY AND SUBSTANCE CORROBORATED IN PRESS. / AWARDEE NAME PER THE STATE SPREADSHEET.'), slide 05's 'SURFACE = MILES FROM THE FAIRBANKS HUB' and slide 06's 'BAR LENGTH LINEAR. ONE PIXEL IS $14,000.' At 432px those are effectively invisible. Slide 04's body also sits below the 32px body floor at 28px, and slide 02's kicker breaks with an orphaned 'FRIDAY' on its own line.

criteria.name: Copy: voice & hook
criteria.notes: Hook lands at 130 chars, inside the 140 fold, on a real definition subversion: data centers and gigawatts against a note taker for about $25,500. 897 chars, inside the 300 to 900 band. Deck summary line present. The close is a genuinely debatable question about an unsupervised task rather than a polite prompt. The voice takes a position ('Seven of the eight hand the decision back to a person. The one that would fly alone got a planning year.') and then discloses its own method twice. Commas at 0.82 per 100 chars against a 1.05 budget, grade 8 to 10. Held off 9 because the fourth paragraph is four short declaratives stacked as disclosure rather than argument, and because the caption never names the August 16th deck it is updating, which is the one callback a returning reader would want.

As it stands storyboard.md still prints '[n/a ] score score_report.json missing' and '[FAIL] ship_gate ... weakest: ?', which is truthful for the moment it was generated but will otherwise ship a false FAIL row and a literal '?' into the run's permanent record for the second round running. 2) CONTRAST, know before posting: primary text is ink at 14.2:1 everywhere, so no gate is breached, but on this white ground the graphite and mono instrument tier measures roughly 2.4:1 to 3.9:1, and slide 03's provenance pair, slide 05's SURFACE line and slide 06's ONE PIXEL IS $14,000 scale note are effectively unreadable at feed scale. If anyone asks where a figure came from, point them at slide 07 and the first comment, not at the small print. 3) SOURCING: five of the eight awardee names rest on the state spreadsheet parse alone (C22, C24, C31, C32, C33). Only the robotic surgery award, the stroke imaging network and the drone planning award are doubly corroborated in press. If a name is disputed, the answer is the Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet, not a news story. 4) The count of eight is this page's own keyword search of award titles and summaries, not a state category, and the seven-and-one split is an editorial reading. Both are on slide 07 and in the caption; do not defend either as a state finding. 5) This is an explicit update to No.35 (August 16th). The update marker is the cover's 'STATE II . REVISED AUGUST 28TH . SUPERSEDES AUGUST 7TH', which is a cartographic metaphor rather than plain language, and the caption never names the earlier deck. If a returning reader connects them, the payoff is slide 08. 6) STORYBOARD DRIFT, harmless but worth one pass: slide 01's dossier text still says the bar reads 400 MI and slide 04's motif table still says 700 MI, while the renders read the measured 550 MI and 650 MI. The renders are right; two lines of dossier prose are stale. 7) The first comment writes dates as 'August 28th, 2026' (ordinal plus year) where brand.yaml prefers 'August 28, 2026' when a year follows. caption_check passed, so this is a preference and not a gate, but it recurs five times in one block. 8) Every dollar is preliminary, the state allows minor adjustments, and a fifth Friday round is still marked TBA, so both the 185 and the eight are a snapshot.
